threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when you’re handed a ticket machine instead of change at the bus stop—locals barely flinch.
Caught a late-night N37 last week; a bloke was arguing with his reflection in the window, swearing it was his ex. Classic Brixton antics.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh falafel wafting through the streets when the market opens, and the chatter of neighbors making plans. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find a spontaneous street concert at any random corner in Kreuzberg, with locals and tourists alike dancing like no one’s watching.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they roll their eyes at the tourist snapping pics of a burrito outside La Taqueria instead of enjoying it inside.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading Muni riders with a ukulele while waiting for the J line at Civic Center. Totally overlooked of the chaos happening around us.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just order a 'café' and expect coffee. Here, it’s either 'café solo' or 'café con leche'—no middle ground.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the maps they hold, still studying the metro lines while the locals just hop on without a second thought.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think googling 'best coffee' will help you find the right spot. It's all about who you know and the whispers in the queue.
Caught a guy on the 333 last night narrating his life story to a bemused cat in a carrier. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a kid selling lemonade at Karl-Marx-Straße, while a couple was having a heated debate about the best Döner in town.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you see people doing yoga on the tram during rush hour, completely unfazed by the chaos around them.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local if they know the best times to avoid Dolores Park when the food trucks show up. Outsiders? They just flock on weekends, clueless about the lines.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit eating a burrito on the bus while an accordion player serenaded the last stop. Only in the TL, folks.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the street performers are just fun, but some are actually locals making a living. It's a fine line between art and survival here.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still look confused trying to figure out the taquilla at the metro. Regulars glide right by.
